text:
Yes, Monzo offers overdrafts on personal accounts in the UK if you're eligible. It's optional, and you apply in the app.

**How it works**
- When you open an account, Monzo checks your credit file to decide whether it can lend to you. This is a soft search, so it won't affect your chances of getting credit.
- If you're offered an overdraft, you can switch it on at sign-up or apply to turn it on later.
- You choose your own limit, up to the amount Monzo can offer you. You can change it at any time in the app or switch it off.

**What it costs**
- The EAR (effective annual rate) depends on your credit score and will be 19%, 29% or 39%. You can see your personal rate in the overdraft section of the app.
- The rate is variable. As an example, an arranged overdraft of £1,200 used for 30 days at 39.0% EAR/APR would cost £32.94.
- Monzo says it doesn't charge hidden or late fees, so its EAR and APR are the same.
- Interest comes out of your account on the first of every month.

**Going over your limit**
- If you go over your arranged limit, you enter an unarranged overdraft, which is charged at the same rate as your arranged one.
- If you have no arranged overdraft and your balance goes below zero, Monzo charges 39% EAR (variable). Unarranged overdraft charges on your current account are capped at £15.50 a month.

**Short-term use only**
- Monzo says overdrafts are for short-term borrowing. If you use yours but add no money to the account for over 60 days, Monzo might ask you to make a payment into it.

Business accounts have separate overdraft terms. The figures above are from Monzo's personal overdraft pages, and the PDF I drew some from is an older version. Check the app for your exact rate before you borrow.
